utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-00-39-T, The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Stewart, I'm informed that the Defence would like to address the Chamber. I take it it is in respect of scheduling. We briefly dealt with the issue in closed session last week, but as I indicated at that time, it's a matter that should be discussed, or at least explained, in open court. Let me just repeat what I said in closed session last week: That the parties have submitted to the Chamber a, let's say, a programme of communications which might lead to considerable savings in court time. The parties would communicate about the facts that took place mainly in the municipalities and at the same time they would discuss to what extent expert reports would be acceptable for the Defence or not and what were the issues still to be dealt with during court hearings. The schedule proposed would at least include not sitting after this week until the summer recess, and in order to continue it would also have consequences for time we would sit in the month of September because not the whole of the programme could be concluded before the summer recess. The Chamber, as I indicated last week, will follow the suggestions of the parties, that is, not to sit in the month of July, but, and I added that as one of the conditions or one of the -- one of the things the Chamber wants to do is to keep a close eye on the progress made during these communications, during these discussions between the parties, because if we finally would spend a couple of weeks on that just at the end to find out that there was not a substantial agreement on some of these facts, we could have used our time better in court to hear the witnesses so that the Chamber would be in a position to form its opinion on the basis of testimony rather than on the basis of agreement between the parties. And I think I indicated that we would like to have our first monitoring moment after the first two weeks of the communications between the parties - that would be approximately the 9th of July - so that we could decide whether we would continue on this path or whether we should go back to hearing witnesses in court. That's what I said. I also said that we would have to discuss this in more detail during open sessions. The Chamber is of the opinion that the public is entitled to know more in detail how the Chamber considers these matters; that is, how much time did we use in court until now, how much time has the Prosecution taken for its case presentation until now, what are the prospects for the near future if we would go the one way or the other way. I'm preparing that to -- well, to further explain what is behind this new proposed schedule. That's what I referred to already last week in closed session and I said what we have to do in open court. I haven't prepared fully yet all the details, the -- well, the statistical data. I'm also looking back at what happened in the last month of 2003 when we discussed the start of the case. I take it that within one or two days I would be ready to fully explain with all the data available. If there's anything apart from that you'd like to raise at this moment, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for that, Your Honour. In fact, that wasn't -- I understood that Your Honour would probably deal with this more fully in a day or so's time, and I wasn't proposing to take time on that issue, but I'm grateful for the indications given. And my simple comment on that this morning is the Defence does strongly favour these matters being fully and openly discussed in open court. We heartily endorse the Trial Chamber's observations that the public at large, whatever section of the public, do have the right to know exactly what is going on and the reasons, and we're grateful that it will be fully discussed and ventilated in open court. So I say no more this morning because clearly that opportunity will arise. Your Honour, rather a more specific immediate point of scheduling: Your Honour, we have found that the scheduling for this week involves sitting every morning. Your Honour, may we say that it isn't all that easy for anybody involved, the Trial Chamber, of course, we recognise, and anybody else, the scheduling. But we had understood until -- in fact, until yesterday -- I'm not quite sure when everything was available to be checked on the internet, but we had understood that we would be sitting in the afternoon on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday this week. That was what was scheduled, and that was what appeared on the printed schedule which we have had in our possession for a long time. When we checked the internet yesterday, we found that we were in the morning, so I don't know exactly when in the course of last week or whenever the change became publicly available. But we were otherwise, apart from any opportunity we had to check it through those channels, we were certainly not notified or consulted of any -- in relation to any such change. Your Honour, often that's no more than a very minor inconvenience, and it's not a huge inconvenience at the moment, but I would like to say that I have myself made some arrangements this week which depended upon, particularly on Wednesday, on the hearing being on Wednesday afternoon. And Your Honour knows from Your Honour's own previous practical experience that such troublesome matters for all concerned as organising with the Registry, travel arrangements and so on, are time consuming and difficult, and they can't always be left until the last minute. So Your Honour -- I want to be actually very open about what is it is, Your Honour. Since we are in open court and we adhere to the principle of publicity, I'll be absolutely frank what it is. I am very pleased to say that my chambers in London are short listed as six chambers for an award of Chambers of the Year for this year, and since I've been absent nearly all the time over the last few months, they have been very keen that I, as one of the Queen's Counsel in those chambers, should attend on Tuesday evening, and I am very keen to go there. It is very difficult to do if I have to be back on Wednesday morning, first thing, to be in court here at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see whether we could change for Wednesday. I mean, being Chambers of the Year, of course, is not something you should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no, but at least there's a fair chance. It's like in the European championships, you never know what the outcome will be. I'll take care that whenever possible, and I think at this moment the court schedule of the Tribunal might be such that there's some flexibility possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would clearly like to add, in the spirit of helpfulness, that if I know what is coming up on Wednesday morning, I wouldn't even, in the circumstances, need necessarily to ask the Trial Chamber to make that adjustment; I would just need to know what was going to happen on Wednesday morning so that it didn't cause trouble for the Trial Chamber and everybody else if I were not here until the middle of the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will see what we can do to accommodate you. Of course, we also have to look at witnesses, we have to look at staff, we have to ask the Prosecution, but we'll do that in between -- Prosecution's now aware of the problem. Prosecution is also presenting the witnesses. So I saw, Mr. Harmon, that you are also a bit impressed by the nomination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That was the idea, I wanted to impress Mr. Harmon, Your Honour. That was the main purpose of my intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel. We, of course, are willing to accommodate counsel in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So whenever possible, we will accommodate you and we will try to get you certainty as soon as possible, I hope even this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And our sympathies to two-thirds of the Bench for the championships mentioned a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stewart. Then, is the Prosecution ready to resume the examination-in-chief of Witness 628 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in closed session? Then I'd like to ask the usher to pull the curtains down, and we'll turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 22nd day of June, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
